question_text: Find the set of x for which the binomial expansion of (2 + 3x)^(−2/3) is valid.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the set — how you take 2 out of the bracket, and the condition on x that makes the expansion valid.
insider_note: The condition is |3x/2| < 1 AFTER the 2 is factored out — never |2 + 3x| < 1. The interval is open: square brackets at the ends lose the mark.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Take out the 2
steps.margin_note: First mark. Factor 2 out so the bracket reads (1 + 3x/2); the negative fractional index changes nothing about the condition.

recall.must_convey: That (2 + 3x) to the power −2/3 is 2 to the power −2/3 times (1 + 3x/2) to the power −2/3, valid when |3x/2| < 1.
accept: take two out to get two to the minus two by three times one plus three x by two to the minus two by three, valid when mod three x by two is less than one
factor out the two so the bracket is one plus something
the expansion is valid when the modulus of three x by two is less than one
two bayataki teeste one plus three x by two, mod three x by two less than one
write it as a power of one plus three x by two

steps.why: Negative or positive, a fractional index gives an infinite series that converges only for |y| < 1 in (1 + y)ᵖ.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus from the index of the 2 outside.

steps.label: Solve for x

recall.must_convey: That |3x/2| < 1 gives |x| < 2/3, so x lies in the open interval (−2/3, 2/3).
accept: mod x less than two by three so x is in minus two by three to two by three
x lies between minus two by three and two by three
the set is the open interval minus two thirds to two thirds
mod x two by three kante takkuva, x minus two by three to two by three
open interval from minus two thirds to two thirds

steps.why: The end points are excluded because the series does not converge at |y| = 1 for this index.
